title: Start here: one backend family, several implementation technologies
summary: The Native Database Backends family presents a stable provider-neutral contract above several implementation technologies. 'Native' is not synonymous with FFI: PostgreSQL may use Foreign Runtime/libpq, GeoPackage has a portable pure-ooRexx direct reader, and process/bridge routes remain explicit fallbacks. Higher layers select by capability, qualification and policy, then pin the chosen implementation for the acquired session/transaction.
invariants: Interchangeability means contract compatibility, not pretending all backends have identical capabilities.
Pure ooRexx, Foreign Runtime and process/bridge implementations are distinct implementation kinds under one upper contract.
Capability and limitation publication is part of the backend contract, not optional documentation.
Fallback is selected before session acquisition; work is never silently replayed through another implementation after session/transaction acquisition.
procedure: Read backend capabilities, limitations, requirements, qualification state and implementation identity.
Select an eligible implementation according to explicit priority/policy.
Acquire and pin that implementation for the session/transaction.
Surface post-acquisition failures rather than replaying through a fallback.

provenance.claim: v0.2 defines a provider-neutral backend family where native may be pure ooRexx or Foreign Runtime, with explicit fallbacks and no vendored dependencies.
